notable_absence.finding: No storage-engine (Couchstore/Magma) mention anywhere despite this page being entirely about bucket and cluster data portability - migration guidance is written as storage-engine-agnostic. No Enterprise/Community edition badges appear either. The page does implicitly reference version constraints ('You can restore bucket backups only to a cluster running the same or later version of Couchbase Server') but never cites a specific version number, so the known 'server-version-string citation' anomaly does not recur here in its usual concrete form.

cross_component_finding: Surfaces a bucket-*type* axis distinct from storage-engine: 'Cluster backups do not capture buckets that use the Memory Only bucket type' - the first explicit naming of a second bucket type alongside the 'Couchbase' bucket type data-service.md (this batch) names, and orthogonal to the Couchstore/Magma storage-engine axis storage-engines.md documents. Also reuses index-state's deferred/Created -> Ready GSI lifecycle enum (originally minted from n1ql CREATE/BUILD INDEX statement pages) in a completely different context - bucket/cluster restore - confirming that enum's applicability spans both DDL-time and restore-time index-state transitions. Role-gating here is uniform and simple: every backup/restore/XDCR method that requires a Capella role requires exactly one, Project Owner - no disjunctive multi-role gate of the kind seen on n1ql CREATE BUCKET (Organization Owner / Project Owner / Data Writer).
